papers.title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
papers.abstract: In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.

papers.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
papers.abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

papers.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.

papers.title: Invariant mean on weakly almost periodic functionals over a Hopf-von Neumann algebra
papers.abstract: Let \(M\) be a Hopf--von Neumann algebra with predual \(M_*\). Using minimal weak*-closed left ideals, we obtain an idempotent state \(\varphi\in\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)^*\) satisfying \(\varphi\star \omega\star\varphi=\varphi\) for every state \(\omega\) on \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\). This state determines the largest closed introverted subspace \(X_\varphi\subseteq\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) containing the identity and admitting a two-sided invariant mean. We also characterize the existence of a unique two-sided invariant mean on introverted operator systems in \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) by a symmetry condition on their left and right state orbits. The criterion recovers the classical results for locally compact groups and their Fourier algebras, and gives a unified treatment of cocommutative Hopf--von Neumann algebras, compact quantum groups, unital \(C^*\)-Eberlein algebras, and \(\operatorname{WAP}(M(G))\) for every locally compact group \(G\).

papers.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

papers.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be induced by a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

papers.title: Cost of one-relator groups
papers.abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.

papers.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
papers.abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.

papers.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
papers.abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's \(L^1\) space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight phi, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence, and make the relationship with the order convergence results of Chetcuti et al. explicit. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local phi-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and \(\|h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}\|_1\to0\) for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming \(\sigma\)-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.

papers.title: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
papers.abstract: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index. We prove that, when the associated subfactor has finite depth, the 3-tensors satisfying the zipper condition correspond precisely to the quantum $6j$-symbols, also known as $F$-symbols, of the unitary multi-fusion category arising from the subfactor. This realization of quantum $6j$-symbols differs from their realization through a flat bi-unitary connection arising from the higher relative commutants of a subfactor.

papers.title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
papers.abstract: For Hermitian matrices $\alpha,\beta$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^\alpha$ and $m$ letters $e^\beta$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)\ge\Tr e^{n\alpha+m\beta}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.

papers.title: Equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for amenable actions
papers.abstract: We prove that every amenable action of a countable discrete group on a separable, simple, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra absorbs the trivial action on $\mathcal{Z}$ up to cocycle conjugacy. The group may be nonamenable, as in Suzuki's recent examples, and no assumptions on outerness or on the tracial state space are needed. This extends OpenAI's result for amenable groups to amenable actions. Amenability of the action cannot be omitted in general, as examples of the author and Lupini show. More generally, we show that every tracially amenable action on a separable, unital, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra with traces admits invariant central copies of all matrix algebras, without simplicity or nuclearity. For amenable actions on simple nuclear algebras, equivariant property (SI) allows one to deduce $\mathcal{Z}$-stability from this. As applications, we obtain absorption of $\mathcal{Z}$ for intermediate subalgebras in the crossed product, and also pure infiniteness for outer amenable actions of nonamenable groups. The basic techniques involving Gaussian variables originate in OpenAI's preprint, and are also the main new tool in its proposed solution to the Toms--Winter conjecture. We extend these techniques in order to deal with the weight functions coming from amenability, and one of the main new ingredients is the fact that one can replace an amenable action by an auxiliary one for which the amenability weights are central. In order to make the probabilistic tools accessible to the community beyond what is used here, we include an appendix where the theory is developed assuming only an elementary background, and where the relevant estimates are proved in detail.

papers.title: The Carpenter property for subfactors of uniform infinite index
papers.abstract: We show that if $N\subset M$ is an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of uniform infinite index, for instance an irreducible inclusion of infinite index, then every positive contraction $b\in N$ is of the form $E_N(p)$ for a projection $p\in M$. This gives the exact version of Popa's asymptotic result in the ultrapower, and it is a subfactor analogue of the Carpenter problem for masas. In particular, Popa's relative dimension set of such an inclusion is $[0,1]$, so the set of expectations of projections does not distinguish inclusions without corners of finite index. As applications, the Carpenter property holds for $N\subset N\rtimes G$ whenever an infinite group $G$ acts outerly on a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$, and for ICC groups $H\le G$ the inclusion $L(H)\subset L(G)$ has it exactly when $[G:H]=\infty$, confirming a recent conjecture. We also give examples showing that the Carpenter property does not imply uniform infinite index, and that infinite index does not imply the Carpenter property.

papers.title: The relative dimension set of an extremal subfactor of finite index
papers.abstract: Popa's relative dimension set $\Lambda(M,N)$ of an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors $N\subset M$ consists of the scalars $\alpha$ for which some projection $p\in M$ satisfies $E_N(p)=\alpha1$. Popa computed it for index at most $4$, and for index $d>4$ outside the middle interval $(t_d,1-t_d)$, where $t_d(1-t_d)=d^{-1}$; whether the middle interval meets $\Lambda(M,N)$ for every irreducible inclusion of index $d>4$ has remained open. We show that for every extremal inclusion of finite index $d>4$, the whole interval $[t_d,1-t_d]$ is contained in $\Lambda(M,N)$. Consequently, $\Lambda(M,N)$ depends only on the index for all extremal inclusions of finite index, in particular for all irreducible ones. Extremality cannot be dropped: for $d>4$, Popa's locally trivial inclusions are exactly those whose relative dimension set misses the middle interval. Other non-extremal inclusions can contain the whole middle interval in their relative dimension set, or miss part of it.

papers.title: Degree and arity of tracial separation for self-adjoint contractions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent explicit counterexample to Connes' embedding conjecture, we study the degree and number of variables needed to separate normalized matrix traces on self-adjoint contractions from traces on finite von Neumann algebras. We prove that the two trace infima coincide for every Hermitian polynomial of degree at most two in at most three variables, with a dimension-explicit approximation bound. We give three explicit separators: an integer-coefficient polynomial of degree six in ten variables with 392 nonzero words, a quadratic polynomial in 214 variables, and an integer-coefficient polynomial in two variables of ordinary and cyclic degree 24. Each has normalized trace at least \(3/4\) on every matrix contraction tuple and trace \(-1\) at a finite tracial witness. We provide the source systems, transfer estimates, and exact coefficient recipes for all three constructions.

papers.title: The Nuclear Dimension of Extensions and Graph $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the nuclear dimension of any graph $C^*$-algebra is at most two, and we compute the exact value of the nuclear dimension for a large class of graph $C^*$-algebras. In particular, this class covers all graphs with Condition (K). Our methods --- based on Szab\'o's recent $KK$-uniqueness theorem --- provide a unified approach to computing the nuclear dimension of various extensions. This includes the nuclear dimension of the Toeplitz algebra (first computed by Brake--Winter) and that of the Cuntz--Toeplitz algebras (first computed by Easo et al).

papers.title: Geometric Aspects of $C^*$-Extreme Points II
papers.abstract: Building on the results of \cite{HR}, we investigate the relationship between \(C^*\)-extremality and linear extremality in the closed unit balls of general unital \(C^*\)-algebras. We show that, unlike in von Neumann algebras, these two notions of extremality need not coincide in general \(C^*\)-algebras. More precisely, we prove that the unilateral shift is a linear extreme point, but not a \(C^*\)-extreme point, of the closed unit ball of the Toeplitz \(C^*\)-algebra. We further establish that \(C^*\)-extremality implies linear extremality whenever the \(C^*\)-algebra admits a faithful unital representation on a separable Hilbert space. We also prove this implication for elements admitting a factorization $x=v|x|$, where $v$ is a partial isometry belonging to the algebra, and extend the result to suitable quotient \(C^*\)-algebras, including the Calkin algebra. Finally, we characterize the linear extreme points of the closed unit ball of unital \(C^*\)-subalgebras of \(B(H)\) containing the compact operators.

papers.title: Frechet differential of a power series in Banach algebras
papers.abstract: We present two new forms in which the Frechet differential of a power series in a Banach algebra can be expressed in terms of absolutely convergent series involving the commutant $C(T):A\mapsto [A,T]$.Then we apply the results to the analytic functional calculus in a complex Banach space.

papers.title: Integral equalities for functions of unbounded spectral operators in Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate a limiting procedure for extending local integral operator equalities to the global ones and to applying it to obtaining generalizations of the Newton-Leibnitz formula for operator-valued maps for a wide class of unbounded operators.

papers.title: A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras
papers.abstract: Let $(X,d)$ be a uniformly locally finite metric space, and $T$ an operator in the uniform Roe algebra $C_u^*(X)$ (or uniform quasi-local algebra $C_{ql}^*(X)$). In this paper, we introduce the concept of limit operators of $T$ on galaxies in the nonstandard extension of $X$, and prove that $T$ is a generalized Fredholm operator with respect to the ghost ideal in $C_u^*(X)$ (or $C_{ql}^*(X)$) if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible, and their inverses are uniformly bounded. In particular, if $X$ has Yu's Property A, then $T$ is a Fredholm operator if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible. Using techniques in nonstandard analysis, our result strengthens a work of \v{S}pakula--Willett \cite{SpW} on the characterization of Fredholmness by using less limit operators.

papers.title: Semiprojective Banach lattices
papers.abstract: We study a norm-controlled notion of semiprojectivity for Banach lattices, testing sequential quotient towers in separable ambient lattices and requiring arbitrarily small norm loss at a fixed stage. For a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space $X$, we prove that $C_0(X)$ is semiprojective if and only if $X$ is compact and an absolute neighbourhood retract. Finite $\ell_1$-sums preserve semiprojectivity, and arbitrary $\ell_1$-sums of $1^+$-projective lattices are semiprojective without any order-unit assumption. By contrast, $\mathbb{R} \oplus_\infty \ell_1$ fails to be semiprojective, showing that neither semiprojectivity nor $1^+$-projectivity is preserved by finite $\ell_\infty$-sums, extensions, or pullbacks over a projective base. Every separable semiprojective lattice is $\lambda$-projective for some finite $\lambda$, and its scalar-valued lattice homomorphisms separate points. Consequently, a separable reflexive Banach lattice is semiprojective precisely when it is finite-dimensional, and no nonzero separable atomless order-continuous lattice is semiprojective. We also characterise $\ell$-openness as $1^+$-projectivity relative to separable ambient lattices; for separable domains this is ordinary $1^+$-projectivity. The restriction to separable ambient lattices is redundant for separable domains but affects the nonseparable examples.

papers.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
papers.abstract: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.

papers.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge 2$. We characterize the nonzero additive maps on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction, assuming surjectivity only in infinite dimension. These maps are precisely those of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is unitary or antiunitary, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar for $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and a nonzero real scalar for $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$.

papers.title: The functoriality of moves on graphs and extended path homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Combinatorics of graphs is a very powerful tool to unravel various properties of graph algebras. In particular, isomorphisms between graph algebras are often implemented by moves between their graphs. In this paper, we make these combinatorial methods functorial. Our categorical approach not only reveals the relationship between moves, but also leads to unexpected extensions of known moves (shifts and reductions) and the characterization of out-splits as admissible epimorphisms admitting a lifting of the source map. The former allowed us to go beyond isomorphisms and Morita equivalences, and the latter yielded a factorization lemma for out-splits. Better still, the functorial understanding of maximal out-splits permitted combining them with the derived-graph construction, which resulted in computing new proper endomorphisms of Cuntz algebras. Finally, the functorial implementation of balanced in-splits required the construction of a new category of graphs, where morphisms are given as homomorphisms of graph inverse semigroups. Thus, the combinatorics of moves brought a new tool to the realm of noncommutative topology where directed graphs are viewed as quantum spaces.

papers.title: How to approximate the flat spectral triple of a quantum torus by fuzzy tori : a twisted tale
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical and the quantum flat torus can be rigorously approximated at a differential level by finite-dimensional fuzzy tori within the framework of the spectral propinquity, a distance up to unitary equivalence which we extend in this paper to the space of twisted, metric spectral triples. Standard attempts to establish this convergence are traditionally obstructed by the intrinsic non-locality of discrete calculus and the subsequent failure of the Leibniz rule. While contemporary alternatives such as spectral truncations circumvent this issue by abandoning $C^*$-algebras in favor of operator systems, our approximations instead remain within the $C^*$-algebraic category, generalizing the commutator formula used to define the Lipschitz seminorm induced by spectral triples. To this end, we introduce a relaxed notion of a twisted spectral triple where the twist is a linear map acting as a discretized Riesz transform that encapsulates the non-locality of the discrete world. Self-adjointness is obtained by adjoining the backward difference to the forward difference and representing this doubled calculus with the creation and annihilation operators of the CAR algebra. The maximum of the norm of the twisted commutator and norm of the displacement of the twist from the identity becomes our Lipschitz seminorm, from which the quantum metric structure of quantum compact metric spaces (QCMS) on fuzzy tori is constructed. Our proposal to connect twisted spectral triples with QCMS recovers the usual connection between metric spectral triples and QCMS. By extending the spectral propinquity to this generalized setting of twisted spectral triples with possibly unbounded twists, we prove that fuzzy tori equipped with their natural two-sided discrete calculus converge to an amplification of the standard flat Dirac triple, while the underlying twists converge to the identity.

papers.title: A Direct Polynomial Approach to Spectral Decomposition
papers.abstract: We give a direct construction of the spectral projectors of a complex square matrix, based on explicit interpolation polynomials previously introduced. This yields a spectral resolution $A=\sum_{i=1}^r(\lambda_iP_i+N_i)$ from which the Primary Decomposition Theorem, the Cayley--Hamilton theorem, criteria for diagonalizability, and the spectral theorem for normal matrices are proved by short formal arguments. A weaker form of the construction, extends to any perfect fields via a Galois invariance argument and produces the Jordan--Chevalley decomposition.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Freeness of Wigner Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, within the framework of real infinitesimal free probability introduced by C\'ebron and the second author, we compute the real infinitesimal free cumulants of independent complex Wigner matrices. Our approach relies on establishing a combinatorial relation between annular non-crossing partitions and families of directed graphs. As a consequence, we demonstrate that independent complex Wigner matrices are asymptotically real infinitesimally free. In particular, we show (under mild conditions) that a complex Wigner matrix is asymptotically infinitesimally free from its transpose.

papers.title: Noncommutative Maximal Averages over Submanifolds and Variable Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish noncommutative maximal inequalities for averages over submanifolds in the $L^p$-spaces associated with semifinite von Neumann algebras. For every $1<p\leq\infty$, we prove local maximal bounds for smooth submanifolds of finite type at the parameter origin, and global bounds over all positive scales for polynomial parametrizations, without a finite-type assumption and with constants depending only on $p$, the degree and the dimensions. For variable hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq3$, satisfying a uniform rotational curvature condition, we obtain local maximal bounds for $p>n/(n-1)$. To our knowledge, these are the first such noncommutative inequalities for general lower-dimensional submanifolds and polynomial images. The key step is a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for a regularized auxiliary family adapted to non-isotropic dilations. The geometric kernels need not satisfy the pointwise smoothness or $L^2$-Dini conditions required by existing noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund theories. We combine a Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition based on Cuculescu projections with integral regularity estimates, a non-isotropic Littlewood--Paley decomposition and Fourier decay to prove this endpoint estimate. Marcinkiewicz interpolation yields maximal $L^p$ bounds for the regularized averages, and interpolation with Fourier-based $L^2$ bounds recovers the original averages. The variable-hypersurface result uses oscillatory $TT^*$ estimates and localization. As applications, we obtain maximal ergodic inequalities for trace-preserving actions of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and, under additional assumptions, bilaterally almost uniform convergence results for the associated normalized averages.
